heroDescription: Trace Minnesota football from its expansion beginnings through Bud Grant's contenders, the Metrodome's passing stars, and an unforgettable playoff finish in Minneapolis.
timelineKicker: From the first kickoff to the Minneapolis Miracle

timeline.title: Minnesota gets its NFL team
timeline.description: The NFL awarded Minnesota a franchise on January 28. The Vikings name followed that September, ahead of the team's debut season.

timeline.title: Tarkenton makes an immediate impression
timeline.description: In Minnesota's regular-season debut, rookie Fran Tarkenton threw four touchdown passes and ran for another as the Vikings defeated Chicago 37–13.

timeline.title: Bud Grant takes the sideline
timeline.description: Grant arrived from Winnipeg to lead Minnesota, beginning the coaching era that would carry the franchise into sustained contention.

timeline.title: An NFL championship before the merger
timeline.description: Minnesota beat Cleveland 27–7 on January 4, 1970, to claim the 1969 NFL title. Kansas City then defeated the Vikings in Super Bowl IV.

timeline.title: A defensive tackle wins MVP
timeline.description: Alan Page became the first defensive player chosen as the Associated Press NFL MVP, earning the award for his 1971 season.

timeline.title: Three NFC crowns in four seasons
timeline.description: The Vikings won the NFC in the 1973, 1974, and 1976 seasons, reaching Super Bowls VIII, IX, and XI under Grant.

timeline.title: Football moves under the dome
timeline.description: Minnesota left Metropolitan Stadium for the Metrodome, trading its outdoor home for an indoor chapter in franchise history.

timeline.title: Moss helps ignite a 15-win season
timeline.description: Rookie Randy Moss caught 17 touchdowns as Minnesota finished 15–1 and scored 556 points. Atlanta ended the run in the NFC Championship Game.

timeline.title: Peterson's remarkable return
timeline.description: After a major knee injury the previous December, Adrian Peterson rushed for 2,097 yards and earned the NFL MVP award.

timeline.title: U.S. Bank Stadium opens a chapter
timeline.description: The Vikings began playing at U.S. Bank Stadium, introducing a new home for Minnesota football in downtown Minneapolis.

timeline.title: The Minneapolis Miracle
timeline.description: On January 14, 2018, Case Keenum found Stefon Diggs for a 61-yard touchdown as time expired, beating New Orleans 29–24 in the Divisional Round.

eras.title: Tarkenton and the outdoor years
eras.description: Metropolitan Stadium framed the early Vikings story: Tarkenton's improvisation, Grant's arrival, and a franchise learning how to contend.

eras.title: The Purple People Eaters
eras.description: Alan Page, Carl Eller, Jim Marshall, and Gary Larsen formed the defensive line associated with Minnesota's tough identity. Page's 1971 MVP season became its defining individual honor.

eras.title: The Metrodome passing show
eras.description: Dennis Green's 1998 team paired Randall Cunningham with Randy Moss, Cris Carter, and Jake Reed. Its explosive offense made a 15–1 season a lasting touchstone.

eras.title: A stadium's first playoff memory
eras.description: U.S. Bank Stadium's first playoff game ended with Diggs racing into the end zone. The Minneapolis Miracle turned one final snap into a shared Minnesota memory.

methodology: This independent guide uses the Vikings' historical archive and Pro Football Hall of Fame records. Season labels identify the football season; January playoff dates are stated separately. The 1969 NFL championship preceded the merger and is distinct from a Super Bowl victory. Player selections span eras and are not a ranking.
